item.title: 2019: Jacob DeGrom Wins Second Straight Cy Young Award
item.description: New York Mets pitcher Jacob DeGrom became the seventh pitcher to win the Cy Young award for the second straight year. He finished the season with an 11–8 record with a 2.43 ERA and a league-leading 255 strikeouts in 204 innings He is also the 20th pitcher and 11th overall to win the award in consecutive seasons. Photo: David from Washington, DC (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2024: Albernaz Promoted to Assistant Manager
item.description: On November 13, 2024, Albernaz was promoted to the role of assistant manager. Photo: Joel Dinda (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2024: Holt Hired as Red Sox Bullpen Coach
item.description: On November 13, 2024, Holt was hired by the Boston Red Sox to serve as their bullpen coach.

item.title: 2023: Espada Promoted to Manage Astros, Succeeding Dusty Baker
item.description: On November 13, 2023, following the 2023 season, Espada was promoted to manage the Astros after the retirement of Dusty Baker, as 25th in franchise history. Photo: Delaywaves (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2023: Hale Hired as Blue Jays Associate Manager Under Schneider
item.description: On November 13, 2023, Hale was hired by the Toronto Blue Jays to serve as associate manager under John Schneider. Photo: Keith Allison from Owings Mills, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2017: Bobby Doerr, 99, Hall of Fame Second Baseman, Red Sox
item.description: Bobby Doerr, 99, Hall of Fame and nine-time All-Star second baseman; the oldest living major league player prior at the time of his death, who played each of his 14 seasons with the Boston Red Sox between 1937 and 1951 before retiring at age 33 due to a back injury, serving later as a scout for the Red Sox from 1957 to 1966, as well as its first base coach and hitting instructor from 1967 to 1969. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 2015: Brett Anderson Accepts Dodgers' Qualifying Offer, $15.8 Million
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Brett Anderson decided to accept his qualifying offer, meaning he will get a one-year, $15.8 million deal for 2016. Anderson joins Colby Rasmus and Matt Wieters in taking the qualifying offer, the first three players to do so since the system started. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2014: Mike Trout, Clayton Kershaw Win MVP Awards
item.description: Mike Trout of the Anaheim Angels earns the American League Most Valuable Player Award, while Clayton Kershaw of the Los Angeles Dodgers deservedly wins the National League honor, marking only the 11th time in Major League history that two players from the same market captured the hardware for the same season. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2014: Alvin Dark, 92, 1948 NL Rookie of the Year, Braves
item.description: Alvin Dark, 92, 1948 National League Rookie of the Year for the Boston Braves and three-time NL All-Star shortstop for the New York Giants, who hit .417 for the 1954 Giants' World Series champions; later managed the San Francisco Giants to the 1962 NL pennant and the Oakland Athletics to the 1974 World Series title; also managed the 1966–1967 Kansas City Athletics, 1968–1971 Cleveland Indians (serving concurrently… Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 2013: Max Scherzer, Clayton Kershaw Win Cy Young Awards
item.description: Max Scherzer of the Detroit Tigers and Clayton Kershaw of the Los Angeles Dodgers are named Cy Young Award winners of the American and National League respectively. Scherzer, Major League Baseball's only 20-game winner at 21–3, receives 28 of 30 first-place votes. Photo: David on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2012: Bichette Hired as Colorado Rockies Hitting Coach
item.description: On November 13, 2012, Bichette was hired to be the Colorado Rockies' hitting coach, replacing Carney Lansford.

item.title: 2010: Marlins Trade Cameron Maybin to Padres for Mujica, Webb
item.description: The Florida Marlins trade Cameron Maybin to the San Diego Padres for Edward Mujica and Ryan Webb. Photo: Djh57 (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2007: Kazuhisa Inao, 70, Japanese Hall of Fame Pitcher
item.description: Kazuhisa Inao, 70, Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame pitcher for the Nishitetsu Lions, who won the Pacific League MVP Award in 1957 and 1958 and posted a 42–14 record in 1961. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1996: Giants Trade Matt Williams to Cleveland Indians
item.description: November 13, 1996: Matt Williams was traded by the San Francisco Giants with a player to be named later to the Cleveland Indians for a player to be named later, Jeff Kent, Julián Tavárez, and José Vizcaíno.

item.title: 1996: Roger McCardell, 64, Catcher for 1959 Giants
item.description: Roger McCardell, 64. catcher for the 1959 San Francisco Giants.

item.title: 1984: Ryne Sandberg Named NL MVP, Cubs' First Postseason in 39 Years
item.description: Ryne Sandberg, whose efforts afield and at bat helped the Chicago Cubs make post-season play for the first time in 39 years as NL East champs, is named the National League's MVP, capturing 22 of 24 first-place votes. Tony Gwynn of the actual 1984 NL pennant-winners, the San Diego Padres, gets one first-place vote and finishes third. Photo: clare_and_ben (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1981: Reggie Jackson, Ferguson Jenkins Among Free Agents
item.description: Forty-one MLB players are granted free agency after playing out their contracts. They include future Hall of Famers Reggie Jackson and Ferguson Jenkins and luminaries such as Joaquín Andújar, Ron Guidry, Rick Monday, Bobby Murcer, Jerry Remy and Reggie Smith.

item.title: 1979: Stargell, Hernandez Named Co-MVPs, First Tie in Award History
item.description: For the first time, there is a tie for the winner of a Most Valuable Player Award. In the National League, Willie Stargell of the world-champion Pittsburgh Pirates and Keith Hernandez of the St. Louis Cardinals are judged co-MVPs by the BBWAA, in custody of the award since 1931. Photo: Sally Lindsay (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1974: Steve Garvey, 25, Wins NL MVP With 200 Hits
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Steve Garvey wins the National League Most Valuable Player Award. Garvey, 25, collected 200 hits, 111 runs batted in, his first All-Star nod, and the first of his four straight Gold Glove Awards during 1974. Photo: Cal Montney, Los Angeles Times (CC BY 4.0).

item.title: 1968: Bob Gibson Wins NL MVP After Cy Young Triumph
item.description: Bob Gibson of the St. Louis Cardinals follows his Cy Young Award triumph by his selection as the National League's Most Valuable Player, taking 14 of 20 first-place votes and 242 points to Pete Rose's six votes and 205 points. Photo: Monowi (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1967: NL President Giles Calls AL Expansion Plan Half-Cocked
item.description: Deriding the American League's 1969 plan to expand to Seattle and Kansas City and adopt divisional play as "half-cocked," NL president Warren Giles vows that the Senior Circuit won't be rushed into such a hasty decision; he denies that his league also coveted the Seattle territory and says NL owners will not consider expansion until the winter meetings convene later this month—at the earliest. Photo: Staff photographer of the newspaper (Public domain).

item.title: 1956: Redlegs Acquire Hacker, Hoak and Whisenant From Cubs
item.description: The Cincinnati Redlegs acquire pitcher Warren Hacker, third baseman Don Hoak and outfielder Pete Whisenant from the Chicago Cubs for pitcher Elmer Singleton and third baseman Ray Jablonski. Photo: Bowman (Public domain).

item.title: 1951: Frantic Frank Lane Keeps White Sox Busy in Trade Market
item.description: The Chicago White Sox remain active in the trade market under general manager "Frantic" Frank Lane, dealing pitcher Randy Gumpert and outfielder Don Lenhardt to the Boston Red Sox for left-hander Chuck Stobbs and infielder Mel Hoderlein.

item.title: 1889: Bridegrooms and Red Stockings Jump to National League
item.description: The Brooklyn Bridegrooms and the Cincinnati Red Stockings jump from the American Association to the National League in the middle of an AA league meeting.
